v1.feedback: The harmattan wind system is well-crafted — cyclic gusts, desiccation palette morph, dust scatter off tips — but the piece is a fresh L-system tree, not a morph of the parent Möbius form. Chain mode requires the parent's topology to remain legible with the word layered on top; a Möbius band being sand-blasted and dried would satisfy both constraints. Keep the wind/palette machinery but apply it to the y3k geometry: twist the Möbius ribbon, scatter particles off its surface edges, let the harmattan erode the band rather than grow an unrelated tree.

v2.feedback: The harmattan concept genuinely drives the shader — edge-particle peel, gust ramp, ochre/sienna/dust palette shift all read as dry wind eroding a Möbius strip rather than decoration bolted onto the parent. Two refinements: the detach factor (2.8 * uGust) at full ramp risks scattering edge particles far enough to dissolve the strip's silhouette into ambient drift — clamp peel displacement or fade alpha toward zero so peeled particles evaporate rather than linger as orphan dots. Second, the high-freq tremor (sin at 9.0, cos at 7.5) is visually noisy at the edges; halving those frequencies or gating tremor behind a stronger edgeDist threshold would keep the shudder legible as wind rather than jitter.
